football_evidence.question: Can Memphis’ pass rush get to Cale Hellums?
football_evidence.assessment: EdgeDesk’s number is 6.1 points closer to Army than the line, and EdgeDesk cannot account for most of that: its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 6.1 points. The measured football evidence leans toward Memphis, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.
supporting: When Army has the ball (the red zone): Army’s offense succeeds on 63.5% of its red-zone plays, and Memphis’ defense allows success on 36.0% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).

When Army has the ball (big plays on the ground): Army’s offense turns 8.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and Memphis’ defense gives up explosive gains on 9.1% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Army has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Army’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 11.8% of its runs, and Memphis’ defense stops 14.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).

When Memphis has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Memphis’ offense has allowed a sack on 7.5% of its dropbacks, and Army’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
contradicting: When Memphis has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Memphis’ offense averages 9.4 yards per pass attempt, and Army’s defense allows 8.7 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
When Memphis has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Memphis’ offense averages 5.8 yards per carry, and Army’s defense allows 6.3 yards per carry (FBS average 5.0).

When Memphis has the ball (big plays through the air): Memphis’ offense turns 12.0% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Army’s defense gives up explosive gains on 13.1% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Memphis has the ball (big plays on the ground): Memphis’ offense turns 7.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Army’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
quarterbacks: Marcus Stokes has completed 150 of 224 passes (67.0%) for 2,169 yards, 9.7 yards per attempt, 22 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in eight games for Memphis, and has been sacked on 15 of 239 dropbacks.
Cale Hellums has completed 39 of 69 passes (56.5%) for 422 yards, 6.1 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 1 interception in seven games for Army, and has been sacked on 3 of 72 dropbacks.
